CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sex: [redacted]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Department: Haematology

CLINICAL DETAILS
Reason for Referral: Suspected acute myeloid leukemia (AML) on bone marrow trephine biopsy
Clinical History: Patient presented with pancytopenia and constitutional symptoms. Bone marrow trephine showed hypercellular marrow with increased blast population suspicious for AML.

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Bone marrow aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Transit Time: 5 days
Specimen Condition: Hypocellular, clotted

TESTS REQUESTED
1. Conventional cytogenetics (G-banded karyotype analysis)
2. Interphase FISH panel for AML

METHODOLOGY
Conventional Cytogenetics: Bone marrow cells were cultured in RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum for 24 and 48 hours. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested using standard protocols with colcemid arrest, hypotonic treatment, and methanol/acetic acid fixation. G-banding was performed using trypsin-Giemsa staining.

Interphase FISH: Due to absence of metaphases, interphase FISH was attempted using the following probe panel:
- CEP8 (D8Z2)
- RUNX1/RUNX1T1 dual fusion
- PML/RARA dual fusion
- CBFB break apart
- MLL break apart

RESULTS

CONVENTIONAL CYTOGENETICS
Result: FAILED - No analyzable metaphases obtained

Technical Details: Despite extended culture periods and multiple harvest attempts, no dividing cells were observed. The specimen was severely hypocellular with extensive cellular degeneration, likely due to prolonged transit time (5 days). Cell viability assessment showed <5% viable cells upon receipt.

INTERPHASE FISH
Result: FAILED - Inadequate probe hybridization

Technical Details: Interphase FISH analysis was attempted on fixed cell pellets. However, probe hybridization was inadequate with <10% cells showing interpretable signals for any probe set. This is attributed to poor cellular morphology and DNA degradation secondary to sample age and transport conditions.

INTERPRETATION
Cytogenetic analysis could not be completed due to technical failure related to specimen quality. The hypocellular nature of the sample combined with the extended transit time (5 days) resulted in insufficient viable cells for conventional karyotyping and poor-quality nuclear material for FISH analysis.

The cytogenetic profile remains undetermined, which limits risk stratification and may impact treatment planning for this patient with suspected AML.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Strongly recommend repeat bone marrow aspirate collection with immediate transport (same day) to the cytogenetics laboratory
2. If repeat bone marrow sampling is not feasible, consider peripheral blood sample if circulating blasts are present (>10% blasts recommended)
3. Ensure sample is collected in sodium heparin (green top) tube and transported at room temperature
4. Collection should ideally be performed before initiation of chemotherapy as treatment may affect cell division and reduce metaphase yield
5. Consider concurrent molecular testing (FLT3, NPM1, CEBPA) which may be performed on non-viable samples

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
Date: [redacted date]
